newsitem.title: USA: Orlando, Fla., airport sees 13.9 pct growth in '96.
newsitem.headline: Orlando, Fla., airport sees 13.9 pct growth in '96.

text.p: Florida's Orlando International Airport saw a 13.9 percent increase in passenger traffic in 1996, the highest growth rate among the world's top 30 airports, the Airports Council International said.

A record 25.58 million passengers used the airport last year. Domestic traffic totaled 23 million, a 15.1 percent rise over 1995. International traffic totaled 2.53 million, a gain of 4.1 percent over the previous year.

"Our airline partners added more destinations and flights for our residents and visitors in 1996, increasing the service available to both business and leisure travelers," said Bob Bullock, Executive Director of the Greater Orlando Aviation Authority.

Orlando International Airport is the 16th busiest in North America, according to Airports Council International's latest ranking. Forecasts project it will serve 30 million passengers by 2000, including more than four million international passengers.
